architecture.approach: Two workspace-level definitions, each owned by one pure module that both sides of the wire mirror. Custom fields: a CustomField document per workspace (unique key), validated by server/src/utils/customFields.ts (coerceFieldValue, planCustomValues, slugFromName) and stored on the task as task.custom[key]; the client mirrors the rules in client/src/features/fields/lib/fields.ts and caches the list per workspace. Workflow stages: an array on the workspace document (workflow.stages) validated by server/src/utils/workflow.ts, where each stage is a refinement of one of the three canonical status groups, and the task's stage and status are resolved together by stageFor on every write; the client mirrors the resolution in client/src/features/workflow/lib/stages.ts and caches the stages per workspace. Definitions change only with settings:manage, values are read with tasks:read, and every cascading effect (clearing removed options, moving tasks off a removed stage, deleting a field) happens inside the same request.

fields.name: projects
fields.type: string[] (<=50 project names, empty = every project)

fields.name: archived
fields.type: boolean (at most 30 not archived per workspace)

fields.name: custom

fields.name: workflow.stages
fields.type: { key, name, group, color, wipLimit }[] (1-12, one stage per group at least)

dataModel.flowDescription: Definitions: a field goes through validateCreateField/validateUpdateField, then the controller slugs the key, enforces the 30-active cap, stores the document and audits it; removing an option or deleting a field runs updateMany over the workspace's tasks with the custom.<key> path to unset or pull the lost choice. Stages live inside the workspace document: PUT /workflow validates the whole list, plans the moves of removed stages, updates the affected tasks in an order that keeps status and completedAt truthful, resynchronises the tasks of a stage that changed group, resets stale stages, clears the legacy board limits and audits the diff. A task write resolves stage and status together through stageFor and validates the custom part through planRequestCustom before the document is saved.     On the client, both definitions are cached per workspace and shared by every view; the settings pages stage their edits locally and publish the server's answer into the same cache.

securityConsiderations.description: Field documents, stage lists and the updateMany calls that clear values are all filtered by the workspace of the request (req.workspace._id); reorderFields also verifies that every id in the body is an ObjectId that belongs to the workspace, and taskQuery.buildTaskFilter only ever writes custom.<key> paths whose key matched the field slug pattern, so a request cannot address another workspace's data or another document's field.

Reading definitions needs tasks:read; creating, renaming, reordering, archiving, deleting a field and replacing the workflow or the board settings need settings:manage, enforced by requirePermission in the routers. The settings pages additionally hide their actions from members without it, which is a courtesy, not the boundary.

A stage can only ever belong to pending, in-progress or completed, and the workflow must keep at least one stage per group, so no configuration can introduce a fourth bucket or leave a report without data for a status.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: Custom values are read from the task document itself (no join), the field definitions are loaded once per request in planRequestCustom and cached per workspace on the client, and the stages travel with the workspace document that requirePermission already loads.

Clearing values is one updateMany per removed option (or per deleted field) over an index-prefixed workspace filter instead of a per-task loop; reordering writes only the rows whose order actually changed.
The list view resolves the columns and the filter choices from the cached definitions, so opening the toolbar or switching views costs no extra request.

risks.description: Duplicated client/server validation can drift and accept different values on each side.
risks.mitigation: Both implementations are pure modules with mirrored unit tests (customFields.test.ts / workflow.test.ts against fields.test.ts / stages.test.ts), the client validates before saving and still shows the API message, and field types and the field key can never be changed after creation, so stored values keep their meaning.

risks.description: A workflow change can strand tasks in stages that no longer exist, hiding them from the board.
risks.mitigation: planStageMoves runs before the save and falls back to the first stage of the group, stale stages are reset, status and completedAt are resynchronised, and resolveStage repairs the display for anything that was written earlier.

risks.description: Deleting an option or a field loses task data without the user noticing.
risks.mitigation: The values are cleared in the same request, the audit entry records how many were cleared, and the settings UI warns before deleting a field.

risks.description: Unbounded definitions would grow every task document.
risks.mitigation: Explicit caps in the model and the validators: 30 active fields, 30 options, 50 projects per field, 500-character text, 20 multiselect values and 5 filters per query.
